basis: Assistant review of saved filename and publisher-label samples, including low-similarity members. Proposals only; no document contents inspected and no verified kind labels created.

S-67790f062ba1.note: Typical and low-similarity examples include Hearing Memo labels. Some labels say only here; validate those independently.

S-04b75a878cb3.note: Hash-prefixed, dated, and descriptive-name variants share Hearing Charter labels in reviewed examples.

S-0b7cbcf93a02.note: The rh suffix and bill references suggest reported bill text. PDF/XML labels alone do not prove this; confirm document headings and retain bill identity.

S-644c4a77ffa6.note: Reviewed labels include Advisory and Hearing Advisory. Check whether all advisories describe hearings rather than other committee activities.

S-f10f688a0411.note: Markup filenames coexist with publisher labels saying Hearing Memo. Keep the broad memorandum proposal and resolve subtype from the document or scoped source page.

S-03999ffa2b96.note: Filenames explicitly contain record_vote; publisher labels are opaque FC/FI numbers. Check the vote record contents.

S-c0bdc5ce463d.note: Bill-reference and legislative-hearing variants have Hearing Memo labels in reviewed samples. Topic and bill numbers do not change the kind.

S-8312c5d48bae.note: FC-13 and similar filenames and labels expose a numbering convention but do not establish a document kind.

S-ed4c2f180a4a.note: Filenames contain fc_memo; sampled link labels say here. Inspect source headings or the first page.

S-09e585d2bdeb.note: BGT filenames are opaque in isolation. Reviewed labels identify Ranking Member Thompson opening statements. Any future rule must retain that publisher/context scope.

S-cb2f9a526c17.note: Typical examples identify committee chairs, while a low-similarity member identifies Supratik Guha. Do not turn WState or this group into a single speaker-role classification.

S-c46027eb84ff.note: FC/OI-number labels and crpt/hmtg prefixes identify a recurring family. Confirm document contents before interpreting the prefix as a report or vote type.

S-9c225a950b92.note: Generic memo filenames have Hearing Memo labels in reviewed examples. Keep the label evidence attached to each record.

S-2849475b8842.note: Advisory labels agree with filenames, including postponed and updated versions. Event type needs separate confirmation.

S-ae2796a4fea4.note: Oversight-hearing variants have Hearing Memo labels in reviewed examples.

S-45910fa4699e.note: PLAW publication identifiers and several Public Law labels support this proposal. The group includes PDF and USLM XML variants; preserve publication and bill references separately.

S-4cdf2060209d.note: CM-memo filenames recur but sampled labels say here. Context or contents must establish the type.

S-cb9ff9b44ceb.note: MPT-memo filenames recur, including a hearing abbreviation; sampled labels say here. Validate the broad kind and subtype separately.

S-701f61cb9c9f.note: HHRG meeting XML names recur with no publisher labels in the reviewed examples. These may require source-record role handling rather than a document-kind rule.

S-6418e8fe2a76.note: HMTG XML names identify a meeting export family. Inspect XML roots before deciding whether these belong among source records.

S-b5b57a4494f8.note: The AP code separates a publisher naming family; it does not establish a new document kind.

H-0088.note: dip.xml, Diaz/DiMuccio names, DIRECTV-DISH material, and DisplayNews.aspx share a group. Repeated dip.xml records inflate apparent document coverage. This is a concrete failure of the tested SVD/HDBSCAN configuration.

H-0034.note: The group combines documentsingle.aspx, a ZIP archive, a Wikipedia exhibit, and hearing-page slugs. Similarity here does not support a shared kind.

H-0661.note: Memo variants recur, but many labels say only here. This useful group does not offset other incoherent density groups.

H-0682.note: Reviewed filenames and some publisher labels agree on Hearing Memo. Do not infer corpus-wide quality from this selected group.

tail: A deterministic SHA-256-ordered sample of ten ungrouped descriptive filenames includes a hearing notice, bill, written testimony, amendment, Truth in Testimony form, participant response, and name-only files. Stored publisher labels can resolve some examples that filename clustering leaves ungrouped. This is a diagnostic sample, not an accuracy estimate.
